label: Fermat's two-square theorem: strict proof dependencies

nodes.label: Fermat's two-square theorem
nodes.statement: For every prime p with p ≡ 1 (mod 4), there exist natural numbers a and b such that a² + b² = p.

verification.note: This node is the proposition type; its proof routes are represented separately.

nodes.label: Fermat theorem via involutions
nodes.statement: The Fermat two-square theorem follows from parity of fixed points of two involutions on a finite set.

verification.note: Kernel-checked local theorem assembled from imported Zagier involution lemmas.

nodes.label: Prime sum-of-two-squares criterion
nodes.statement: A prime p is a sum of two squares when p = 2 or p ≡ 1 (mod 4).

verification.note: General criterion is a planned comparison target.
The proposition is formalized; the explicit-witness proof route is checked separately.

nodes.label: Parity of fixed points of involutions
nodes.description: Two involutions on the same finite set have fixed-point counts congruent modulo two.

verification.note: Provided by the imported Lean development.

nodes.label: Gaussian integers
nodes.description: Representing a + bi as an integer pair with multiplicative norm.

verification.note: Used as the conceptual Gaussian-integer foundation.

nodes.label: Integer lattice circle
nodes.description: A lattice point (a,b) lies on the squared-radius n circle exactly when a² + b² = n.

verification.note: The geometric encoding is defined and checked locally.

nodes.label: Arctangent of a lattice slope
nodes.description: The direction of a lattice vector is recorded by arctan(y/x), with tangent recovering the rational slope.

verification.note: Uses mathlib's tangent/arctangent identity. The identity is a surface-level geometric dependency; its foundational mathlib route may transitively use exp, which should be recorded by extraction rather than duplicated here.
Public source imported by the checked local route.

nodes.label: Involution/fixed-point parity
nodes.method: Build a finite set with two involutions, compare fixed-point parity, and extract a two-square witness.

nodes.label: Geometric lattice point
nodes.method: Represent 29 by the lattice point (5,2), identify its circle radius through the norm, and record its direction by an arctangent slope.

verification.note: A checked geometric/arctangent benchmark; it is not yet a proof of the general prime theorem.

nodes.label: Gaussian integer Euclidean descent
nodes.method: Use unique factorization or Euclidean descent in ℤ[i] to force a representation by the norm form.

verification.note: Route is registered but not yet proved locally.
